Title: Home-Based Aerobic Interval Training Improves Peak Oxygen Uptake Equal to Residential Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Randomized, Controlled Trial
Author: Moholdt et al.
Comment: Final-value data were selected because Table 2 reports arm-level mean, SD, and analysed N at six months. M_diff was computed as home-based AIT minus residential rehabilitation (1.4 − 1.6 = −0.2 mmol/L) for this simple two-group comparison. No unit conversion or Wan imputation was needed. The paper reports EMM changes but not change-score SDs.
domain: Cardiac rehabilitation after coronary artery bypass surgery
Study Environment: Home-based aerobic interval training versus supervised residential rehabilitation at the Feiring Heart Clinic
Medium: Home-based exercise and centre-based residential rehabilitation
Topic of Content: Cardiac rehabilitation and aerobic interval exercise
Participant type: Adults who had undergone coronary artery bypass surgery
Recruitment source: Patients undergoing coronary artery bypass surgery
Outcome measurement: Venous blood after a 10-hour overnight fast; blood lipids analysed using Vitros 350

Title: Effects and costs of real-time cardiac telerehabilitation: randomised controlled noninferiority trial
Author: Maddison et al.
Comment: Outcome-specific analyzed Ns for triglycerides were not reported in the supplied Results text or tables, so arm Ns and total N are left null; randomized group sizes (82 and 80) were not substituted. SE_diff was derived from the reported 95% CI as (0.22 − (−0.34))/3.92 = 0.142857. Values are already in mmol/L, so no conversion was applied. The arm-level values are final 12-week values, not change scores.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('REMOTE-CR (intervention)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA: missing F-value or group sizes
Design Type: Two-arm parallel randomized controlled non-inferiority trial
Study Environment: REMOTE-CR performed remotely/home-based; comparator delivered under supervision in cardiac rehabilitation clinics in Auckland and Tauranga, New Zealand
Medium: Bespoke smartphone app, chest-worn wearable sensor, web platform, and real-time audio coaching for REMOTE-CR; face-to-face clinic supervision for CBexCR
interaction_type: Real-time remote physiological monitoring and individualized exercise coaching versus supervised centre-based exercise coaching
Participant type: Clinically stable adults with documented coronary heart disease within 6 months
Recruitment source: Metropolitan hospitals, outpatient clinics, and community-based cardiac rehabilitation seminars in Auckland and Tauranga
Outcome measurement: Final 12-week fasted blood triglyceride concentration measured with a point-of-care analyser

Title: Program Participation, Exercise Adherence, Cardiovascular Outcomes, and Program Cost of Traditional Versus Modified Cardiac Rehabilitation
Author: Joseph J. Carlson, Jeffrey A. Johnson, Barry A. Franklin, and Ronald L. VanderLaan
Comment: Final-value triglyceride data are reported at 6 months. Apply the specified fixed conversion factor to both means and SDs for synthesis. No triglyceride-specific between-protocol test statistic or p value is reported. The paper notes differential attrition, with the 6-month TP sample representing more compliant participants. No Wan estimation was needed because means and SDs were directly reported.
Medium: Facility-based and independent/off-site exercise cardiac rehabilitation
Topic of Content: Comprehensive cardiovascular risk reduction through exercise, nutrition education, and support
interaction_type: In-person rehabilitation with telephone follow-up in the modified protocol
Participant type: Low- to moderate-risk adult cardiac patients aged 35–75 after cardiovascular surgery or event
Recruitment source: First-time referrals to a cardiac rehabilitation program at a metropolitan hospital
Outcome measurement: Venous blood triglyceride concentration after instructions to fast and abstain from vigorous exercise for at least 12 hours and avoid alcohol for at least 72 hours

Title: Effectiveness of Three Models for Comprehensive Cardiovascular Disease Risk Reduction
Author: Gordon et al.
Comment: Values are 12-week changes from baseline (mean ± SD), not final triglyceride concentrations. This comparison shares the same centre-based control arm with the community-based comparison; synthesis must account for the shared comparator. The paper gives no exact triglyceride-specific between-group F statistic or p value. Multiply both means and SDs by 0.01129 to convert mg/dl to mmol/L.
domain: Cardiac rehabilitation and cardiovascular risk reduction
Study Environment: Centre-based cardiac rehabilitation comparator versus physician office/telephone-supported home-based program in Savannah, Georgia
Medium: In-person office visits and telephone follow-up supporting home-based exercise versus supervised centre-based exercise
Topic of Content: Comprehensive coronary artery disease risk-factor reduction
interaction_type: Physician/nurse office visits and nurse case-manager telephone visits
Participant type: Low- or moderate-risk adults with coronary artery disease
Outcome measurement: Fasting serum triglycerides measured at baseline and after 12 weeks
